## 3. The file inside pi-ai that turns tool-result bytes into model content

$ awk over <pkg>/dist/api/anthropic-messages.js
  995	function convertToolResult(msg) {
  996	    return {
  997	        type: "tool_result",
  998	        tool_use_id: msg.toolCallId,
  999	        content: convertContentBlocks(msg.content),
  1000	        is_error: msg.isError,
  1001	    };
  1002	}
  ** the named lane-2 site: convertToolResult, which places the payload through
  convertContentBlocks into a structured tool_result block keyed by tool_use_id.

$ awk over <pkg>/dist/api/transform-messages.js
  49	    const normalizedMessages = messages.map((msg) => (msg.content == null ? { ...msg, content: [] } : msg));
  176	        else if (msg.role === "toolResult") {

  178	            result.push(msg);
  line 49 is the independent corroboration that pi itself normalises a content-less

## 4. Classification and what it means for the invariant

  Classification: not-decidable. Dependency-tree-only: no fork, no vendored copy,
  no patches/ directory, no pnpm.patchedDependencies hook, no editable TypeScript.

  > The invariant is enforced on one of the two lanes only.
  Lane 1 (pi-claude-cli) is enforced at packages/pi-claude-cli/src/tool-result-authority.ts,
  reached from toolResultContentToText in prompt-builder.ts. Lane 2 (direct OAuth /
  raw API key) would need its own enforcement at
  @earendil-works/pi-ai@1.1.0 -> dist/api/anthropic-messages.js:995 convertToolResult,
  a site neither owned repository can edit.

  Owner-facing decision this card cannot make: ask the upstream pi-ai maintainer for
  the rule, or re-express it engine-side before the payload reaches pi-ai (the
  engine's own import sites, e.g. packages/engine/src/pi.ts, are where such a
  pre-pass would live). Either is a request to another owner, not a patch to land.
